Definition: from G3908; a deposit, i.e. (figuratively) trust:--committed unto.
BiblicalUsage: Paratheke is a deposit, a trust committed to someone's keeping. Paul tells Timothy in 1 Timothy 6:20 to keep that which is committed to thy trust, and in 2 Timothy 1:12 he says he knows whom he has believed and is persuaded that God is able to keep that which he has committed unto Him. In 2 Timothy 1:14 the charge turns back: keep by the Holy Ghost the good thing committed unto thee.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gospel is a deposit, not a possession: God keeps what I commit to Him, and I keep what He commits to me. That is why I hold that the faith is handed on like a trust, and the keeper will be asked what he did with it.
